title: Studio job receipts
question: What did the Media Studio production job table actually record per model and kind: saved, failed, unknown, saved-job latency and the cost estimate that was written on the row?

source.access: Read-only SQL through wrangler. No write, deployment, media fetch or private field in the output.
source.schemaCommand: npx wrangler d1 execute media-studio --remote --command "PRAGMA table_info(generations)" --json
source.sql:
WITH live AS (
  SELECT model, kind, status, created_at, cost_estimate_micro, provider_charged_micro,
         CASE
           WHEN status = 'saved' AND completed_at IS NOT NULL THEN completed_at
           WHEN status = 'cancelled' AND cancelled_at IS NOT NULL THEN cancelled_at
           ELSE NULL
         END AS terminal_at
  FROM generations
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
), saved AS (
  SELECT model, kind, terminal_at - created_at AS elapsed_ms,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY model, kind ORDER BY terminal_at - created_at) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY model, kind) AS n
  FROM live
  WHERE status = 'saved' AND terminal_at IS NOT NULL
), costs AS (
  SELECT model, kind, cost_estimate_micro,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY model, kind ORDER BY cost_estimate_micro) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY model, kind) AS n
  FROM live
)
SELECT l.model, l.kind,
  COUNT(*) AS jobs,
  SUM(l.status = 'saved') AS saved,
  SUM(l.status = 'failed') AS failed,
  SUM(l.status = 'unknown') AS unknown,
  SUM(l.status = 'cancelled') AS cancelled,
  MIN(l.created_at) AS first_created_ms,
  MAX(l.created_at) AS last_created_ms,
  SUM(l.terminal_at IS NULL) AS without_terminal,
  (SELECT (MAX(CASE WHEN s.rn = (s.n + 1) / 2 THEN s.elapsed_ms END) + MAX(CASE WHEN s.rn = (s.n + 2) / 2 THEN s.elapsed_ms END)) / 2.0
     FROM saved s WHERE s.model = l.model AND s.kind = l.kind) AS saved_median_ms,
  (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN s.rn = (9 * s.n + 9) / 10 THEN s.elapsed_ms END)
     FROM saved s WHERE s.model = l.model AND s.kind = l.kind) AS saved_p90_ms,
  SUM(l.cost_estimate_micro) AS cost_estimate_sum_micro,
  (SELECT (MAX(CASE WHEN c.rn = (c.n + 1) / 2 THEN c.cost_estimate_micro END) + MAX(CASE WHEN c.rn = (c.n + 2) / 2 THEN c.cost_estimate_micro END)) / 2.0
     FROM costs c WHERE c.model = l.model AND c.kind = l.kind) AS cost_median_micro,
  SUM(l.provider_charged_micro IS NOT NULL) AS provider_charge_rows
FROM live l
GROUP BY l.model, l.kind
ORDER BY jobs DESC, l.model
source.examplesSql:
WITH picked AS (
  SELECT kind, model,
         json_extract(request_json, '$.aspect') AS aspect,
         json_extract(request_json, '$.durationSeconds') AS duration_seconds,
         json_extract(request_json, '$.aspectRatio') AS aspect_ratio,
         json_extract(request_json, '$.outputWidth') AS output_width,
         json_extract(request_json, '$.outputHeight') AS output_height,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY kind ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM generations
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'saved'
)
SELECT kind, model, aspect, duration_seconds, aspect_ratio, output_width, output_height
FROM picked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY kind

scope.deletedReason: One row has its media erased (deleted_at set). It is excluded from every count and is not described here.

timing.saved: completed_at - created_at, both recorded on the row.
timing.failedOrUnknown: Not measured. The generations table records no completed_at or failed_at on these rows, and updated_at is not a terminal timestamp, so no failure latency is inferred.
timing.cancelled: No cancelled row exists in this window.
timing.clock: Wall-clock elapsed milliseconds, including queue and provider time. It is not compute time and not time to first view.

cost.label: estimate recorded by Studio, not an invoice
cost.note: No row in this window records provider_charged_micro, so no charge or invoice is claimed.

usage.note: The generations table records no token or credit usage for these media jobs, so this page claims none.

groups.inventoryNote: The 16 November studio-media inventory does not list this Studio-only footage-edit route. The production table still records a saved job for it, and this page does not invent an inventory row.
The job row stores the key studio-draft; the inventory lists the same route as studio-draft-retired because new work must not select it.

examplesNote: The newest saved job of each kind in the same window. Only the settings listed on the row are shown; a setting the row did not record is omitted, not filled in.
limits: This is reliability and latency evidence, not a quality ranking. A saved job proves an output was stored; it does not prove the output was good.
No blind human preference between these outputs has been recorded yet, so no model is called better on this page.
The window is 86 jobs over two days on one Studio account and one Cloudflare account. It is not a provider-wide benchmark.
Failed and unknown rows have no terminal timestamp, so their latency is unmeasured rather than inferred from the last edit.
Every cost is the estimate recorded on the job row. No provider charge is recorded on any row, so none of these numbers is an invoice.
Most rows record an aspect and, for video, a duration; pixel dimensions are recorded on one failed job only, so resolution is not compared.
Some routes have a single saved job. A percentage over one job describes that job, not a stable rate.
The Studio model key is the recipe route, not the provider endpoint. The studio-media inventory owns the endpoint mapping.
